The '''dot product''' is a particular instance of an [[inner product]]. It generalises the product of scalar numbers to vectors in $\mathbb{R}^n$.

== Formal definition ==

For $\vec{a}=(a_1,a_2,\cdots,a_n),\vec{b}=(b_1,b_2,\cdots,b_n),\in\mathbb{R}^n$

The '''dot product'''
$$
\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}
=
\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i b_i
$$
<ref>{{#cite:Q2328}}</ref>
{{Hidden example}}
For $\vec{a}=(1,3,-5)$ and $\vec{b}=(4,-2,-1)$,

$$
\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}
=
(1)(4)+(3)(-2)+(-5)(-1)
=
4-6+5
=
3.
$$
{{End hidden}}
